# HAProxy (HTTPS) — root-context

App at /, HAProxy terminates TLS on https://localhost:9443/ and forwards over plain HTTP to the backend. No X-Forwarded-Proto rule is needed: the shared base derives it from the bind's TLS state. `bind ssl crt` loads the key from <crt>.key beside the certificate, so the existing fixture is reused under a second name. The bind offers HTTP/2 through ALPN.

Proxy URL on `https://localhost:9443`: `/`

## Configuration

See [docker-compose.yml](./docker-compose.yml) for service definitions.

HAProxy config (`haproxy/https/root-context/vaadin.cfg`), mounted as
`conf.d/10-vaadin.cfg`:

```haproxy
# App at /, HAProxy terminates TLS on https://localhost:9443/ and forwards over
# plain HTTP to the backend.
#
# Shorter than both HTTP siblings would suggest, and the missing line is the
# interesting part: there is no X-Forwarded-Proto rule here. The shared base
# derives it from the bind's TLS state with
# `set-header X-Forwarded-Proto %[ssl_fc,iif(https,http)]`, which is true for
# every scenario in the tree at once. Compare
# `RequestHeader set X-Forwarded-Proto "https"` in
# apache-httpd/https/root-context/vaadin.conf and
# `proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-Proto $scheme` in
# nginx/https/root-context/default.conf.template.
#
# The bind offers HTTP/2 through ALPN by default, as Traefik's TLS entryPoint
# does and unlike the NGINX sibling's `listen 443 ssl`, which is HTTP/1.1 only.
# WebSocket upgrades still happen over HTTP/1.1, since HTTP/2 forbids the
# Connection and Upgrade headers; browsers open a separate h1 connection for
# them. Worth knowing when reproducing anything by hand: curl negotiates h2 and
# silently drops an Upgrade header unless it is given --http1.1, which makes a
# broken config look fine.
frontend vaadin-in from vaadin-front
    # No key file here: `crt` takes a PEM that may carry the key, and when it
    # does not, HAProxy loads <crt>.key from beside it. The compose file mounts
    # the repo's existing tls/localhost.key under that name.
    bind :443 ssl crt /usr/local/etc/haproxy/tls/localhost.crt
    default_backend vaadin-app

backend vaadin-app from vaadin
    server vaadin vaadin:8080
```

The `global` section, and the two `defaults` sections this file
inherits from, come from the shared
[haproxy-base.cfg](../../haproxy-base.cfg), mounted read-only beside
it as `conf.d/00-base.cfg`. Base and scenario only parse as a pair.
